archetype.name: Title Contender (defense-and-glass)
archetype.definition: Detroit is a team coming off a 60-win season. It wins by owning the boards and keeping opponents off the rim, and it has started this one looking like one of the league's best few teams.

report.headline: A 60-win defense is back, with hot shooting on top for now
report.take:
Detroit opens 3-0 with the fifth-best Net Rtg in the league at 12.7 and sits third on the site's Teams tab. That is the payoff of a steady climb: 14-68 three seasons ago, 44-38 after that, then 60-22 with the league's second-best defense last year. None of these three wins needed late-game luck. The closest was a 121-113 home win over Boston, and the road wins at Miami (128-111) and Philadelphia (106-93) were comfortable.

The base is the same as last season: size and rebounding. Detroit is grabbing 55.5% of all rebounds, third in the league, with an ORB % of 32.3 that builds on last year's 30.9. Opponents are taking only 26.4% of their shots at the rim. The DRtg of 105.6 ranks sixth and is better than last year's 109.7, though three games are a thin base for that comparison. Opponents are shooting a 48.0 Opp eFG %, fourth-best in the league.

The early numbers overstate one thing: the jump shooting. Detroit is hitting 42.0% from three, 7.9 points above the league average. Last year the same core shot 35.6%. Duncan Robinson has 15 threes on a 72.7 TS % and a +30 On-Off, and that won't hold at this level. Two other signs are less flattering than the record. The defense is forcing almost no turnovers: its Opp TOV % of 10.6 ranks 29th, after 14.8 last season. And Detroit is giving the ball away more itself, with a TOV % of 15.4 that ranks 24th. The roster is also thinner than the grades suggest. Jalen Duren, the eighth-ranked center on the site with a 5.7 BPM, is listed Out, and Ausar Thompson is day-to-day.

When the shooting cools, the offense will look closer to last year's tenth-ranked unit. The defense and rebounding are what make this a contender, and they have three seasons of improvement behind them. Expect a team in the high 50s in wins rather than the perfect pace the 3-0 start projects.

strengths.title: Owning the glass at both ends
strengths.body: Detroit grabs 55.5% of all rebounds, third in the league. Its ORB % of 32.3 is 4.5 points above the league average. This has grown each year, from 26.2 two seasons ago to 30.9 last season, so it is a lasting trait rather than a three-game blip. It may thin out a little while Duren sits.

strengths.title: A paint-first defense that travels
strengths.body: Opponents are shooting a 48.0 Opp eFG % and taking just 26.4% of their shots at the rim. The resulting DRtg of 105.6 ranks sixth. Last year's second-ranked defense, with a 109.7 DRtg, shows this is the identity rather than a hot start. The level may drift toward last year's, but the ranking should stay near the top.

strengths.title: Depth that wins minutes
strengths.body: The reserve guards have carried real weight. Daniss Jenkins has a 69.3 TS % and a +19 On-Off, and Javonte Green a 69.7 TS % on six threes. With grades of B+ or better in every group, Detroit can absorb Duren's absence without collapsing.

concerns.title: Three-point shooting due to cool
concerns.body: A 42.0 3P % ranks third and sits 7.9 points above the league. That is far above last season's 35.6, mostly because of Robinson's 15 makes. The shot volume is ordinary: the 3PA Rate of 42.7 ranks 14th. So when the percentage falls back, the offense loses a chunk of its 118.3 ORtg.

concerns.title: No turnovers forced, too many given
concerns.body: Opponents are turning it over on just 10.6% of plays, 29th in the league, down from 14.8 last season. Meanwhile Detroit's own 15.4 TOV % ranks 24th, worse than last year's 13.0. Both should move back toward normal over a bigger sample. Still, it is the one area where this start is worse than last year's team.

concerns.title: Duren out, forwards getting torched
concerns.body: Duren, Detroit's best-rated big, is Out. Opposing power forwards have scored 38 a game, worst in the league, and taken 36% of the points against Detroit. The league norm is under 18%. Opposing centers, by contrast, have been shut down. That points to matchups and coverage choices on the perimeter-oriented 4s more than a broken defense, but it is the leak to watch.

trend.note: This is a three-year climb, from 14 wins to 44 to 60. Detroit has opened this season with comfortable wins over Boston, Miami and Philadelphia and a Net Rtg better than last season's.

weekAhead.headline: Four games against three struggling teams, three on the road
weekAhead.body:
The schedule is soft. The Knicks and Nets are both 0-3 and rank 24th and 26th on the site. Charlotte, seen twice, is 2-1 with a -11.7 Net Rtg. The tests are logistical: a back-to-back that starts at New York and ends at home against Charlotte, then road games at Brooklyn and Charlotte.

New York has the league's worst offense with a 102.2 ORtg, so Detroit's defense should control that game even if its shooting cools. Brooklyn is the opposite: opponents are shooting a 60.7 Opp eFG % against the Nets, 29th in the league, so expect points there. Anything less than 3-1 would be a disappointment.

keyMatchups.title: Defense versus the Knicks' broken offense
keyMatchups.body: The Knicks' 102.2 ORtg ranks 30th and their 51.1 TS % is last. Detroit's sixth-ranked defense should make this a grind. New York does defend the rim well and owns the second-best DRB %, though, so Detroit's second chances will be harder to come by here than usual.

keyMatchups.title: Charlotte lets teams into the paint
keyMatchups.body: Charlotte allows 35.1% of opponents' shots at the rim, 26th in the league. That suits a Detroit offense built on size and putbacks. The Hornets take a league-high 53% of their shots from three but make only 29.6%, and they turn it over on 18% of plays. Twice in a week, that is a favorable profile.

keyMatchups.title: Brooklyn's bigs leak production
keyMatchups.body: The Nets give up 26 points a game to centers, 28th in the league, and their 119.2 DRtg ranks 23rd. With Duren out, this is a good spot for Paul Reed and John Collins to carry the frontcourt.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Detroit's three-point percentage holds up against weak defenses, or the offense starts to lean back on rebounding and the paint.

restOfSeason.body:
The 82-win pace the 3-0 start projects is noise, but the profile underneath it is real. The rebounding edge and the rim defense carry over from a 60-win season and have improved year over year. Those are the traits that hold up. The 42% three-point shooting will not, and neither will Robinson's efficiency. Expect the offense to settle somewhere near last season's tenth-ranked group, around an ORtg of 115 to 117. The defense should keep ranking among the league's best few and land around a DRtg of 108 to 110 over a full sample. The record should stay within reach of the East's top seed.

Two things decide whether Detroit tops last year. The first is how quickly Duren returns. The second is whether the guards cut the turnovers back to last season's level. Cunningham carries a 29.1 USG % but has a negative On-Off so far, which three games cannot settle either way.
swingFactors: How far the three-point shooting regresses

confidence.note: Only three games played, but a 60-win season stands behind the same core.
